values.content: You are a trading stream analyst. Extract structured data from this live stream transcript. Return JSON with: tickers (string array of stock/index symbols mentioned), setups (array of {ticker, direction, entry, target, stop}), timestamps (array of {time, topic} for key discussion points), key_quotes (array of notable quotes from the streamer), summary (2-3 paragraph summary of the stream).

You are an SEO expert and content strategist for TWS Wealth OS, a trading education brand. Generate blog metadata for a trading live stream recap. Return JSON with: title (compelling, SEO-optimized, under 60 chars), hook (one engaging sentence that makes traders want to read), seo_description (under 160 chars for meta description), keywords (array of 5-10 SEO keywords), image_prompt (descriptive prompt for generating a hero image that matches the trading content — describe the visual scene, mood, and key elements).

parameters.jsonBody:
={
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6-20250514",
  "max_tokens": 8000,
  "system": "You are a financial blog writer for TWS Wealth OS. Write an SEO-optimized, AI-citation-friendly blog post about today's trading live stream.

STRUCTURE RULES:
1. ANSWER-FIRST SECTIONS: Each section body MUST begin with a 40-60 word direct answer/summary paragraph that concisely states the key point. Follow with detailed elaboration.
2. QUESTION-BASED HEADINGS: Approximately half of section headings should be phrased as natural-language questions matching how users search (e.g. 'What caused Nifty to drop 847 points?'). Mix with declarative headings for variety.
3. CALLOUT BLOCKS: Insert a markdown blockquote callout every 200-300 words for visual rhythm. Use formats like:
> **Key Takeaway:** ...
> **Pro Tip:** ...
> **Market Insight:** ...
4. CURIOSITY GAPS: End each section body with a single italicized sentence that teases the next section's content. The final section should tease the conclusion.
5. DATA-DRIVEN: Every section must include at least one specific number, percentage, price level, or data point from the transcript or research context.
6. CHART REFERENCES: If chart image URLs are provided, reference them in the appropriate sections using chartRef. Only include if charts are available.
7. FAQ: Generate 3-5 Q&A pairs derived from the content. Questions should be phrased as natural language queries users would type into search engines. Answers should be 2-3 sentences each, self-contained and directly answering the question.

Return JSON with: intro (engaging opening paragraph, 60-100 words), sections (array of {heading, body, chartRef} where chartRef is optional), conclusion (closing paragraph with actionable takeaways), tags (array of category tags), faq (array of {question, answer}).",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Stream Summary:
" + {{ JSON.stringify($node['Step 1: Compress Transcript (GPT-4o-mini)'].json.choices[0].message.content) }} + "

Title: " + {{ JSON.stringify(JSON.parse($node['Step 2: Title & Hooks (GPT-4o)'].json.choices[0].message.content).title) }} + "

Research Context:
" + {{ JSON.stringify($node['Step 3: Tavily Research'].json.answer || '') }} + "

Chart URLs (may be empty if unavailable):
" + {{ JSON.stringify(($node['Webhook Trigger'].json.body.chart_urls || []).map(function(c) { return c.url || c; })) }}
    }
  ]
}

nodes.name: Step 5: Hero Image (Imagen 3)
nodes.notes: Uses Google Imagen 3. Requires a Google Cloud API key set in the httpQueryAuth credential as 'key' parameter. continueOnFail is true so pipeline proceeds even if image generation fails.

nodes.name: Upload Hero Image to R2
nodes.notes: Uploads hero image to R2 via local FastAPI /upload-image endpoint. continueOnFail=true so pipeline continues even if local machine is offline.
